text_blocks.snippet: Central Illinois residents are frequently targeted by active local scams including fake local business impersonations, deceptive government text messages, and fraudulent utility or city notices.

list.snippet: Impostor Repair Services: Scammers set up fake websites and phone numbers posing as trusted local businesses (such as regional garage door repair companies) to overcharge customers heavily for simple fixes.
Secretary of State Texts: Phishing text messages falsely claim to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or DMV, threatening license suspension or unpaid traffic fines to steal personal data.

City and Utility Impersonation: Fraudsters send fake invoices or official-looking letters—such as phony notices targeting residents who recently appeared before local zoning boards—to demand immediate payments.
Storm and Home Repair Fraud: Door-to-door scammers and fake contractors canvas neighborhoods after severe weather offering rushed repairs or high-pressure inspections without valid credentials.
Verify Phone Numbers: Double-check contact numbers independently rather than clicking the top sponsored search result when searching for local service providers.
Ignore Threatening Texts: Remember that state agencies like the Illinois Secretary of State will never text residents demanding payment or threatening immediate license suspensions.
Confirm Official Notices: If you receive a bill or notice from a local municipality like Pekin or Springfield, call their official city hall number directly to verify.
